correctness.rationale: PASS. Orbits of each g on vertices of M_{2n} form a signed independence-polynomial problem: invariant independent sets have no internal-edge orbit and pairwise nonconflicting orbits; the reduced trace equals minus its signed orbit-quotient polynomial. For rotations of step r, quotient orbit length L even forbids every vertex orbit by antipodal edge; L odd gives M_h with h=gcd(2n,r), and a 3-state transfer matrix with eigenvalues i,-i,1 and end swap yields I(M_{2m};-1)=i^m+(-i)^m-1. For reflections the admissible orbit quotient is a two-row ladder with precisely ceil(n/2) or floor(n/2)-1 columns, depending on axis; the evaluation recurrence A_j=-A_{j-2}, A_0=1, A_1=-1 handles n=2 empty case. Agarwal–Basak's independent homotopy theorem concentrates reduced homology in degree d(n) with rank 1 or 3. Multiplying the signed fixed-simplex count by (-1)^d yields the stated 1-dimensional characters and W_square⊕eta_k rank-three action; they satisfy the D_{2n} relations. Independent exhaustive invariant-set enumeration on every rotation/reflection n=2,...,10 reproduced all predicted Lefschetz values, including the n=2 K4 boundary. This does not certify the all-n transfer and fold derivation by finite data.
